 Judgment

The claimants in MVC.No.2775/2010 on the file of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Gokak (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') have preferred MFA.No.100534/2021 seeking enhancement of compensation, while the insurer- respondent No.3 has preferred MFA.No.101958/2020 challenging its liability and quantum of compensation awarded vide judgment and award dated 14.10.2019.
2.
The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

Smt. Laxmi @ Jayashree W/O Vittal Naik vs Sayyed Murtuja S/O Sayyedkhadarpasha ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137296611/
4 3.

Brief facts of the case are that the wife and the children of the deceased Vittal Naik have filed the claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, the 'M.V.Act') claiming compensation from respondent Nos.1 to 3- they being the owner, driver and insurer of the truck bearing Reg.No.KA-29-9156.
Respondent No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
It is contended that the deceased Vittal was riding the motorcycle on 04.04.2010 from Hirenandi to Gokak.
The driver of the truck bearing Reg.No.KA-29-9156 had parked the vehicle by the side of the road without parking lights On.
Without noticing the said truck, the deceased hit the motorcycle on hind portion of the truck.
As a result of which, he died.
The claimants being the wife and children are claiming the compensation.

The mother of the deceased is arrayed as respondent No.4.
5.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed objections denying the contentions of the claimants.
It is contended that the accident had occurred only due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased and therefore they are not liable to pay any compensation.
Even otherwise it is contended that the truck is insured with respondent No.3 and therefore it is respondent No.3 who is liable to pay the compensation.

6. Respondent No.3 filed the objections denying the contentions of the claimants and also contended that the driver of the truck was not holding valid and effective driving NC:
2023:KHC-D:7340 licence and therefore the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

7. On the basis of all these pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed:
"1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 04-04-2010 at about 15-00 hours when Vittal Balappa Naik was returning from Gokak on new Splendor Motor cycle towards Hirenandi village near Ishwarling temple Dundanatti Truck Reg.No.KA-29/9156 was parked on the main road without parking light & the motorcycle has dashed to the Truck & caused the accident by which Vittal died as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, at what amount &
from whom?
3. What order or award?"
8. The claimants have examined PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to 16 in support of their contentions.
Respondents have examined RWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R1 to 5 in support of their defence.

9. The Tribunal after taking into consideration all these materials on record, answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and held that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,45,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of the petition till payment.
The NC: 2023:KHC-D:7340 amount of compensation is apportioned between the petitioner Nos.1, 2 and 3 in the proportion of 50:25:25.

Smt. Laxmi @ Jayashree W/O Vittal Naik vs Sayyed Murtuja S/O Sayyedkhadarpasha ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137296611/
5 10.

Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred MFA.NO.100534/2021 seeking enhancement, while the insurer has preferred MFA.NO.101958/2020 challenging its liability and also quantum of compensation.

11. Heard Sri. Sanjay S.Katageri, learned counsel for the appellants, Sri. Bahubali N.Kanabaragi,
learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2, learned counsel Smt. Anusha V.Sangami for Sri.
S.K.Kayakmath, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
12.
Learned counsel for the appellants- claimants contended that the Tribunal has committed an error in taking the income of the deceased at only 1/3rd of his annual income i.e., Rs.40,000/-.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and award calls for interference.

He also submits that the mother of the deceased was not allotted any share in the compensation and he fairly submits that 10% of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7340 compensation amount to be awarded to the mother of the deceased, who is arrayed as respondent No.4.
13.

Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer submitted that since the driver of the truck had parked the vehicle by the side of the road, there was no negligence on his part and therefore the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

She also contended that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding exorbitant compensation towards loss of consortium, loss of love and affection, loss of guardian to the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 which are not permissible under law.
It has also awarded interest at 9% per annum which is also not permissible, therefore she contends that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for interference.

14. Perused the materials on record.
15.

In view of the above, the point that would arise for consideration is:
- 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:7340  Whether the impugned judgment and  award passed by the Tribunal requires  interference?

16. My answer to the above point is partly in the affirmative in favour of the insurer for the following:

6 REASONS 17.

It is not in dispute that the claim petition filed is under Section 163A of the M.V.Act, where the claimants are not required to plead or prove the negligence on the part of the deceased or on the part of the vehicle involved in the case.

The claimants have produced Exs.P1 to 11- the documents relating to the criminal case initially registered against the deceased as well as the driver of the truck in question and the case against the deceased was abated, but charge sheet was came to be filed against the driver of the truck in question for having parked the truck without any indication.
These documents prove the involvement of the vehicles and the factum of accident.

Thus, the claimants and respondent No.4 before the Tribunal are entitled for compensation under Section 163A of the M.V.Act.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7340 18.
As per post mortem report, the age of the deceased was 24 years.
As per Schedule-II, the income of the deceased could be taken at Rs.40,000/- per annum and the appropriate multiplier would be "17".

Further, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal expenses and hence the annual income of the deceased would be Rs.26,667/-(i.e., Rs.40,000 less 1/3 [personal expenses]).
Thus, the claimants are entitled of Rs.4,53,339/- (i.e., Rs.26,667 X 17 [multiplier]) towards loss of dependency.
The claimants are also entitled for Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards consortium and Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate.

Therefore they are entitled for compensation as under:
Sl.No. Heads Amount  (In Rupees)
 1. Loss of dependency 4,53,339.00
2 . Funeral expenses 2,000.00
3. Loss of consortium 5,000.00  4. Loss of estate 2,500.00  TOTAL 4,62,839.00  - 12 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:7340 19.
They are also entitled for interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

20. The wife of the deceased being claimant No.1 is entitled for 40%, both the children who are claimant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for 25% each and the mother- respondent No.4 is entitled for 10%
of the compensation amount.

Smt. Laxmi @ Jayashree W/O Vittal Naik vs Sayyed Murtuja S/O Sayyedkhadarpasha ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137296611/
7 21.
It is the contention of the insurer that the rider of the motorcycle himself was negligent and therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The very fact that the claim petition was filed under Section 163A of the M.V.Act makes it clear that the claimants are not required to plead and prove the factum of negligence on the part of any of the parties.
Mere use of the motor vehicle which results in road traffic accident is sufficient to invoke Section 163A of the M.V.Act.
Hence, I do not find any merit in the contention raised by the learned counsel for the insurer.
Accordingly, the same is rejected.
However, the contention of the learned counsel for the insurer that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant amount of compensation gains support.
In view of the above, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,62,839/- as against Rs.7,45,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, I answer the above point partly in the affirmative in favour of the insurer- respondent No.3 and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1) The appeal in MFA.No.100534/2021 filed by the claimants is dismissed.
2) The appeal in MFA.No.101958/2020 filed by the insurer is allowed in part.

3) The impugned judgment and award dated 14.10.2019 passed in MVC.NO.2775/2010 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.,
Gokak is modified.

It is held that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,62,839/- as against Rs.7,45,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realization.

It is held that the wife of the deceased being claimant No.1 is entitled for 40%, both the children who are claimant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for 25% each and mother- respondent No.4 is entitled for 10% of the compensation amount.
Office to draw the award accordingly.
Amount in deposit if any, is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of judgment and award.

SD/-

In view of the above, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,62,839/- as against Rs.7,45,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

ORDER 1) The appeal in MFA.No.100534/2021 filed by the claimants is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the contention of the insurer that the rider of the motorcycle himself was negligent and therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
The very fact that the claim petition was filed under Section 163A of the M.V.Act makes it clear that the claimants are not required to plead and prove the factum of negligence on the part of any of the parties.
Mere use of the motor vehicle which results in road traffic accident is sufficient to invoke Section 163A of the M.V.Act.
